answer: Each close the protocol caps one address at 25% of a head's share; last close it clipped 1,120 of 2,302 heads and repooled 301,732,835 POA, 40% of the answer pool, so a farm splits into keys to dodge it. Cap the kin cluster instead, reading the cluster off the funding and referral links the protocol already records: one allowance, split across the cluster, and each head's shortfall over its share burned. The second key in a grove of kin already forfeits half its claim, the tenth nearly all of it, so no honest head is pushed off the ledge. A sonnet is cheap; a clipped one is not.
